subject: docs/coop/artifacts/deferral.DR-110.preview.v2.json
reviewClass: independent, refute not confirm; D-001/D-002 explicit-deferral candidate
summary: This is the only one of the five that D-002 burdened with named authoring requirements, and it meets both: it draws the DR-107/G18 generation-rollback versus self-update-rollback boundary in its own section, and it addresses file 02's unexercised updates inventory entry. The G18 collapse the prompt attacks is refused rather than committed — G18 crash-safety is admitted to the preview precisely because it is not self-update. One advisory: alone among the five, this candidate states no bound on a later slice, so nothing in it says the deferral stops covering DR-110 once self-update is in scope.

advisoriesList.location: The artifact as a whole — absent reentry field, and condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded
advisoriesList.observation: The candidate never says what happens when a later slice adds self-update. I checked this across all five candidates rather than against my own expectation, and the other four each carry the bound somewhere: DR-108 and the Windows candidate both have explicit reentry clauses that state the deferral 'does not cover' the later slice, DR-116's condition-2 effect ends 'Does not cover a later slice that admits third parties', and the DR-106/109/113 candidate limits its effect to 'the named row only' and adds a severability clause. This one has no reentry field, and its condition-2 effect stops at 'May count as the explicit preview deferral D-002 requires for DR-110, including the G18-versus-self-update boundary. Does not SATISFY the row.' Nothing false follows from the omission — scope is set to 'architecture preview (D-002 / D-018) only' in every candidate, so the deferral is slice-bounded by construction. But this is the row whose subject matter most invites the misreading, because self-update is a feature that arrives in a later slice rather than a policy that stays excluded, and a recorded disposition that does not name its own expiry is the kind of text a future reader treats as settled. It is an advisory rather than a blocker because the bound is implicit in scope and because owner recording, not this draft, is the operative act.
advisoriesList.repair: Add the sentence the sibling candidates carry, in the form DR-108 uses: a later slice that ships self-update or repair-media trust re-enters DR-110 as OPEN for that slice, and this deferral does not cover it.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: b6b678dc18dc0ff506d8a96cbf90246b3e84d99cd2a3387032124a153eb5fc52, three measurements at the start and two at the close, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- throughout. The prompt held at 6a46241c… across start and end.

D-002 imposed two specific requirements on this disposition and both are met, which I checked against D-002's own sentence rather than against the artifact's account of it. D-002 reads: 'The DR-110 disposition, when authored, must draw the DR-107/G18 generation-rollback versus self-update-rollback boundary and address file 02's unexercised "updates" inventory entry (turn-3 observation).' The artifact carries a dedicated boundaryWithDR107G18 field for the first, and disposes of the second in two places — 'File 02's updates inventory entry stays unexercised in the preview' and, in whatMustNotBePretendedSettled, 'File 02 updates inventory as a preview ship obligation'.

The attack 'collapses G18 generation rollback into self-update' fails, and the artifact does the opposite of collapsing them. Its boundary section states that DR-G18 and DR-107 'cover generation, lock, lease, and removal crash-safety for preview local state' and 'do not cover self-update or repair-media rollback of the distribution core', then names itself as that boundary. The admission in whatMayBeDesigned is correspondingly qualified — 'DR-G18 crash-safety for preview generation/lock/lease/removal, which is not self-update' — so G18 stays inside the preview on its own terms rather than by borrowing DR-110's deferred surface. That matters because DR-G18 is one of the eighteen required-now gates, so a deferral that swallowed it would have removed a required gate from the slice.

The commission is D-002's own: the explicit-deferrals paragraph names 'DR-110 (self-update/repair — install is fresh signed download in slice 1)', and the artifact's decision reproduces exactly that — 'Preview install is a fresh signed download.'

The attack 'pulls deferred surface into preview' fails on the four-item exclusion list: core self-update, repair-media trust, revocation-aware rollback of an already-installed core, and the file-02 updates inventory as a ship obligation are all held outside, and the decision names crash-injected repair as OUT.

The attack 'coordinator pretending to be owner' fails. ownerWhoMustRecord reads 'Release + platform owners (file 08 DR-110). Coordinator may draft', and I verified the owner string against the register: file 08's DR-110 owner cell reads 'Release + platform owners', matching character-for-character. The effect is conditional throughout — condition2EffectIfOwnerRecorded, and reversibility 'Total before owner recording'. This candidate omits the explicit 'D-000 does not make the coordinator those owners' sentence that DR-108 carries, but it names the owner, conditions every effect on owner recording, and the review prompt states the principle globally, so nothing is loosened.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL, and both SATISFIED occurrences are refusals. DR-110's live lead label is OPEN and this artifact does not touch it. whatThisDoesNotDo also refuses to name a repair-media harness, which is the specific overreach available to this row.

The attacks 'authorizing implementation', 'amending D-002' and 'file 08 edited' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses implementation and file-08 edits, nothing in the text purports to change D-002's deferral set, and file 08 measures 45dc4611… unmodified in my working tree.

The attack 'stale recordedInputs' fails. COORD 4ec06988… and file 08 45dc4611… both equal live bytes at the start and again at the close, and the remeasuredAfter marker f7ce35ff… resolves to 'D-093: record committed host-effect-authorization.v8 candidate'.
The frozen v1 predecessor is unedited: deferral.DR-110.preview.v1.json hashes 838aeb1571f794630977157b8072c8b430fcedaca7b089fabe34dd4325e010c4, matching predecessorSha256.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read.
File 02's updates inventory entry itself. I verified that D-002 required the disposition to address it and that the artifact does so in terms; I did not open file 02 to confirm the entry's wording.

Whether DR-G18's crash-safety scope is correctly drawn for preview local state. I verified the artifact keeps it distinct from self-update, which is what the attack turns on, not that the G18 scope is right.
Whether deferring self-update is the right product call. D-002 made that choice.
The other four deferral candidates, which are reviewed in their own verdict files.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of all five subjects and the prompt three times at the start and twice at the close, with ls -l for permissions; extraction and whitespace-unwrapping of D-002's explicit-deferrals paragraph and its DR-110 authoring requirement from COORD; column-parse of file 08 for the DR-110 owner cell and lead label; sha256 of the frozen v1 predecessor; git log at full hash for the remeasuredAfter commit; structured comparison across all five candidates for reentry fields and later-slice bounds, which is how the advisory was found

acceptNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at zero blockers. D-002 gave this disposition two homework problems and it did both, which is more than the other four had to do. The G18 question is the one I expected to find mishandled, because admitting G18 crash-safety to the preview while deferring rollback is exactly where a boundary gets blurred; instead the artifact makes the distinction its own named section and qualifies the admission inline. The advisory is the mirror image — having drawn a careful boundary in space, the candidate draws none in time, and it is the only one of the five that does not.
